The Tata Group is India's largest business group. It began in 1868, when Jamsetji Tata, a Parsi merchant in Bombay, set up a trading firm.

Jamsetji moved from trade into industry. He built cotton mills, starting in Nagpur in 1877, and opened the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel in Bombay in 1903. He also planned a steel works, a hydroelectric company and a science institute, all finished after his death in 1904:

  • Tata Steel at Jamshedpur, which made its first steel in 1912.
  • The Tata hydro power company.
  • The Indian Institute of Science in Bangalore.

Under J. R. D. Tata, who led it for over fifty years, the group started India's first airline in 1932, later Air India, and built a computer services firm, Tata Consultancy Services, in 1968.

Since India's economic liberalisation in 1991 it has spread abroad, buying Britain's Jaguar Land Rover in 2008, and in 2022 it bought back Air India. Charitable trusts own most of the holding company, Tata Sons. The family belongs to the Parsi community that grew from the Zoroastrians who settled in Gujarat.
sum: The Tata Group is India's largest business group. It began in 1868, when Jamsetji Tata, a Parsi merchant in Bombay, set up a trading firm.
